historical_references.reference: The name Shareef means 'noble' or 'generous' in Arabic. Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab (581-644 AD), one of the Rashidun caliphs, was given this title due to his generous and just rule.

Another historical figure known as Shareef was the Moroccan ruler Abd al-Haqq II (1578-1603). He assumed the title 'Shareef al-Mahdoum' which translates to 'The Noble One, The Forgotten'. He was a part of the Saadi Dynasty and is remembered for his military prowess and patronage of arts and sciences.
